name: Matter of A-B-
holding: (1) Matter of A-R-C-G-, 26 I&N Dec. 338 (BIA 2014) is overruled. That decision was wrongly decided and should not have been issued as a precedential decision.

(2) An applicant seeking to establish persecution on account of membership in a 'particular social group' must demonstrate: (1) membership in a group, which is composed of members who share a common immutable characteristic, is defined with particularity, and is socially distinct within the society in question; and (2) that membership in the group is a central reason for her persecution. When the alleged persecutor is someone unaffiliated with the government, the applicant must also show that her home government is unwilling or unable to protect her.

(3) An asylum applicant has the burden of showing her eligibility for asylum. The applicant must present facts that establish each element of the standard, and the asylum officer, immigration judge, or the Board has the duty to determine whether those facts satisfy all of those elements.
(4) If an asylum application is fatally flawed in one respect, an immigration judge or the Board need not examine the remaining elements of the asylum claim.
(5) The mere fact that a country may have problems effectively policing certain crimes or that certain populations are more likely to be victims of crime, cannot itself establish an asylum claim.
(6) To be cognizable, a particular social group must exist independently of the harm asserted in an application for asylum.

(7) An applicant seeking to establish persecution based on violent conduct of a private actor must show more than the government's difficulty controlling private behavior. The applicant must show that the government condoned the private actions or demonstrated an inability to protect the victims.
(8) An applicant seeking asylum based on membership in a particular social group must clearly indicate on the record the exact delineation of any proposed particular social group.

(9) The Board, immigration judges, and all asylum officers must consider, consistent with the regulations, whether internal relocation in the alien's home country presents a reasonable alternative before granting asylum.
summary: Matter of A-B- was issued by Attorney General Sessions, during the first Trump administration. This is an example of the lesser common types of immigration case law: decisions plucked from the standard appeals process, BIA > District Court > Supreme Court, and is decided by the Attorney General.
notes: The procedural history of this case is 'a lotta ins, a lotta outs'. It's an incredibly powerful, sweeping set of decisions. For a cryptic overview of its history and eventual replacement by, well, the case law that preceded it (Matter of A-R-C-G-), see here: https://www.justice.gov/eoir/page/file/1404796/dl

name: Matter of H-A-A-V
holding: If the factual allegations underlying a claim for asylum, withholding of removal, or protection under the Convention Against Torture, viewed in the light most favorable to the respondent, do not establish prima facie eligibility for relief or protection, an Immigration Judge may pretermit the applications without a full evidentiary hearing on the merits of the claim.

name: Matter of K-E-S-G
holding: A particular social group defined by the alien's sex or sex and nationality, standing alone, is overbroad and insufficiently particular to be cognizable.
summary: This is higly relevant and impactful case law, in that PSG formulations such as 'Mexican women who XYZ' become immediately subject to a request for pre-termission by DHS.

name: Matter of A-L-S-
holding: (1) Flight risk encompasses not only whether a respondent is likely to appear at future hearings, but also whether the respondent is likely to comply with future orders of the Immigration Judge.
(2) Speculative future eligibility for relief does not materially diminish a finding of flight risk.
summary: Nuanced and specific: in A-L-S, the BIA reiterates the importance of flight risk for an IJ considering issuing a bond, and emphasizes that the mere fact that the respondent may have relief should not 'materially' reduce the risk of flight. While this may sound niche, many bond cases are borderline cases already.

name: Niz-Chavez v. Garland
holding: For purposes of triggering the stop-time rule for cancellation of removal, the government must serve a single Notice to Appear containing all statutorily required information. The required information cannot be supplied through multiple documents served at different times.
summary: Of tremendous significance to both practitioners, especially Respondents' counsel, as this Supreme Court decision further clarifies the way in which a person must be notified of the commencement of removal proceedings against them (through service of a Notice to Appear), as well as to Language Nerds, because this decision goes extremely hard regarding the murky grammar of the English language.

In any case, TL;DR: an NTA has to consist of one single, atomic, unitary document that includes both notice that the named person must appear for immigration proceedings, as well as the place, date, and time of that initial appearance. This sounds stupid and like 'yeah of course duh?' but, uh... It's harder to make a valid NTA than you would expect.

name: Matter of Buri Mora
summary: Addresses the 'exceptional and extremely unusual hardship' standard applicable to non-lawful permanent resident cancellation of removal under INA §240A(b).
notes: Clarifies application of the hardship standard. In particular, the existence of a qualifying relative's medical diagnosis, standing alone, does not automatically establish exceptional and extremely unusual hardship; the hardship determination remains a fact-intensive inquiry.

name: Matter of Josefina ARAMBULA-BRAVO, Respondent
holding: (1) A Notice to Appear that does not specify the time and place of a respondent's initial removal hearing does not deprive the Immigration Judge of jurisdiction over the respondent's removal proceedings.

(2) A Notice to Appear that lacks the time and place of a respondent's initial removal hearing constitutes a “charging document” as defined in 8 C.F.R. § 1003.13 (2021), and is sufficient to terminate a noncitizen's grant of parole under 8 C.F.R. § 212.5(e)(2)(i)(2021).
cites: Pereira v. Sessions, 138 S. Ct. 2105 (2018), and Niz-Chavez v. Garland, 141 S. Ct. 1474 (2021), distinguished; Matter of Bermudez-Cota, 27 I&N Dec. 441 (BIA 2018), and Matter of Rosales Vargas and Rosales Rosales, 27 I&N Dec. 745 (BIA 2020), followed.
summary: The next installment in the ongoing series, 'what is a notice to appear, anyway?', Arambula-Bravo specifies, among other things, that parole granted upon entry to the country is extinguished upon issuance of the NTA. This has additional consequences that may not be immediately apparent; it can, for example, change a certain legal status of a respondent, e.g. from 'arriving alien' to 'entered without inspection'. This can have effects on bond proceedings, sometimes preventing, or sometimes allowing for, bond to be set.

name: Matter of C-A-R-R-
holding: An Immigration Judge is not required to consider an Application for Asylum and for Withholding of Removal (Form I-589) on the merits if it is incomplete, and an incomplete application may be considered waived or abandoned, particularly where the respondent has been given an opportunity to cure the deficiency.

A declaration is not a constituent part of an asylum application. An Immigration Judge therefore may not deem a Form I-589 incomplete or abandoned solely because the respondent did not submit a declaration.
summary: C-A-R-R- addresses some conditions under which an Immigration Judge may treat an asylum application as incomplete and thereby consider it waived or abandoned. The I-589 itself--the actual freaking form, not a supplement pointed to with a note like 'see supplement'--must contain substantive answers to every question.

Importantly, however, a separate written declaration is not itself a required constituent part of Form I-589. Failure to submit a declaration therefore does not, standing alone, make the asylum application incomplete.
notes: This is, in a way, a long time coming, and represents a tremendously powerful tool for the DHS to request pre-termission of cases, thereby clearing out the cases that, `on their face`, are highly unlikely to prosper on their merits. The other tool, or horseman of the apocalypse depending on your politics, is Matter of H-A-A-V-, which addresses whether the facts alleged by the respondent in their application, even if accepted as true, establish prima facie eligibility for relief. One interesting thing to consider is the existence, in Spanish administrative law / case administration, of the legal figure 'aceptar a trámite'. This is a binary yes /no initial decisoin, generally made by a judge or similarly positioned legal expert, as to whether the case meets certain prima facie levels of sufficiency on given criteria. In a way -- if we can step back for a second -- the idea that the US Immigration courts went forward with a full hearing on applications that were wildly incomplete and whose alleged fact patterns clearly match existing case law barring the relief requested -- is a bit insane.
